summary: Snohomish County, WA: a 1930s lookout cab (no tower) near the 6,989-ft peak; gone by 1950, when a USGS party found nothing; no source describes the site today.

notes_for_editor: Only one source describes the lookout itself in any detail (the Register's one-line description, repeated on firelookout.com). Willhite's page is a climbing guide to White Chuck Mountain, not a lookout page, and it is where the brief's source list points; it contains the inventory citation, the 1950 USGS visit and his doubt that a summit lookout existed. The brief's kind 'ground' and elevation 2130.2 m are consistent with the sources, so no corrections are proposed. The 1930s build date is given only as a decade, so no build event is recorded. The peak is spelled Whitechuck Mountain by the register and Forest Lookouts and White Chuck Mountain by Willhite. Used 4 page reads and 0 WebSearch calls.
